title: A Provision for the Summit
premise: Juniper Villalobos has spent nine years running her riverboat, the Marisol, up and down the Río Cobre, outrunning debts, memories, and the family she left behind. When a survey expedition led by cartographer Elias Thorne goes silent above the Gorge of Whistling Stones, she is the only captain willing to make the run — and what she finds is not wreckage but survivors, including a stowaway boy who carries a map everyone upstream wants buried. Hunted by the mining consortium that financed the expedition and racing the first snows across the Cordillera del Viento, Juniper must choose between delivering the map for the bounty that could free her from her past or protecting the ragtag found family that has formed aboard her boat. She chooses them, burns the map at the summit pass, and finally stops running — steering the Marisol home to the town she once abandoned.
about_author: Coral Ashgrove is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight runs on inland waterways before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. Her fiction is known for its riverine settings, weather-worn characters, and stubborn belief that people can choose their own families.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Juniper pilots the Marisol through dawn fog on the lower Río Cobre, reading sandbars by instinct while dodging a debt collector waiting at Port Salinas. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness; she refuses a mooring offer because staying means being found.

chapters.title: A Cargo of Silence
chapters.summary: Hired to carry supplies to the expedition basecamp, Juniper notices the crates are labeled for a mining survey, not mapping. A quiet boy, Tomás, hides among the cargo. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: unease hardening into suspicion; she recognizes the look of someone running.

chapters.title: Radio Weather
chapters.summary: At basecamp, expedition leader Elias Thorne pays in promises instead of coin, and Juniper overhears him arguing about 'what's under the ridge.' That night the radio crackles with an unfinished distress call from upstream. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: dread arriving ahead of the storm.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Juniper runs the Gorge of Whistling Stones against every warning, Tomás unexpectedly proving a gifted spotter. They find the expedition's overturned tender and one survivor: injured botanist Mara Quill, clutching a sealed oilskin case. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Oilskin Case
chapters.summary: Mara reveals the expedition found an ancient highland route — and evidence the consortium plans to dam the valley and drown three villages. The case holds the only full map. POV: Mara (first of several). Emotional beat: guilt; Mara sent the distress call that now endangers them all.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Juniper wants to dump the problem at the next port; instead she finds herself feeding refugees from a burned village who beg passage. Tomás quietly claims Mara as kin. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the reluctant first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: Consortium Men
chapters.summary: A black-hulled launch shadows the Marisol; its captain, Renard, offers Juniper triple pay for the case and hints he knows about her brother's debt back in Port Salinas. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: Nine Years Downriver
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: why Juniper fled — the flood she failed to prevent, the family that blamed her, the debt she inherited. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: understanding that her wandering was always penance, not freedom.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Leeward Side
chapters.summary: Renard's men torch a fuel depot, stranding river traffic and forcing Juniper toward the overland route. Mara's wound turns feverish. POV: Tomás. Emotional beat: a child deciding these adults are his to protect.

chapters.title: The Porter's Road
chapters.summary: They hire muleteers in San Vega and begin the climb into the Cordillera del Viento, carrying the disassembled Marisol's irreplaceable engine parts as trade goods. POV: Mara, feverish and lucid by turns. Emotional beat: leaving the river means losing the identity that kept her safe.

chapters.title: Whistling Stones, Singing Pass
chapters.summary: A mountain guide, old Ilsa Berríos, recognizes the ancient route on a glimpse of the map and warns it is sacred ground the villages' ancestors used to escape exactly such men. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: history rhyming; the past offering a path forward.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: First snow falls early. Renard's party closes to half a day behind. Juniper considers surrendering the map to save the group and hates herself for considering it. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Village Under the Ice
chapters.summary: They shelter in ruins beneath a glacier and find carvings matching the map's symbols — proof the route was made by people fleeing a dam-building empire centuries ago. POV: Tomás. Emotional beat: belonging to something older than blood.

chapters.title: Renard's Parley
chapters.summary: Renard catches them at a bridge, wounded and outnumbered, and makes his final offer: the map for their lives, plus Juniper's debts erased. Mara urges giving it up; the truth can be told without paper. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the argument that splits the found family.

chapters.title: What Juniper Owes
chapters.summary: Juniper nearly signs — until she realizes Renard's contract would make the villagers' testimony worthless in court. She tears it up. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: choosing people over absolution.

chapters.title: The Bridge Fight
chapters.summary: A desperate night skirmish on the rope bridge; Ilsa cuts it behind them, falling with two of Renard's men. They escape but lose their mules and most supplies. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: grief priced into every mile gained.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Blizzard traps them in a snow cave for three days on short rations. Stories are traded like food: Juniper tells the truth about the flood; Tomás admits he stowed away to find the sister Renard's men took. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: truth as the glue loyalty was pretending to be.

chapters.title: Tomás's Sister
chapters.summary: Clearing skies reveal Renard's camp below — with prisoners, including Tomás's sister Luz. Juniper plans a rescue she knows may cost them the summit window. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the found family committing fully to its own.

chapters.title: The Summit Window
chapters.summary: Climax begins: a dawn raid frees Luz and the villagers' captured spokesman, but the pass will close within hours. Renard pursues onto the glacier. POV: alternating Juniper and Tomás. Emotional beat: terror and fierce joy braided together.

chapters.title: Burning the Map
chapters.summary: Cornered at the crest, Juniper burns the oilskin map before Renard's eyes — the route lives now in the memories of those who crossed it. Renard, exposed to his consortium as holding nothing, retreats. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: liberation through loss.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: The survivors cross the pass as the snows seal it behind them, carrying testimony that will sink the dam project in court. Ilsa's death is mourned properly, in her own village's rite. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: sorrow carried openly, together.

chapters.title: Home Water
chapters.summary: Spring: the Marisol is reassembled and steams upriver to Port Salinas, where Juniper settles her brother's debt face-to-face and asks forgiveness she doesn't demand. Tomás and Luz stay aboard. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the runner drops anchor — belonging chosen at last.
